subject: physics
title: Electrical power and the heating effect of current
key_idea: **Power** is the energy transferred each second. Electrical power is P = IV or P = I²R. A current heats a resistor because electrons collide with the ions in the lattice and make them vibrate more.

blocks.text: Power links the energy changes in a circuit device to the potential difference across it and the current in it.

items.meaning: The energy transferred per second. It is measured in watts, W.
The unit of power. One watt is one joule per second.

blocks.label: Power from potential difference and current
blocks.formula: power = potential difference × current    (P = V I)
where: potential difference, V, in volts, V
current, I, in amperes, A (amp is acceptable)

blocks.label: Power from energy and time
blocks.formula: power = energy transferred ÷ time    (P = E / t)
where: energy transferred, E, in joules, J

blocks.text: Use P = I²R when you are given the current and the resistance but not the potential difference. Square the current before you multiply.

diagram.alt: Change the current and the resistance of a device and see the power for P = I x V and P = I squared x R.

blocks.text: For the same resistance, double the current and the power goes up four times, because the current is squared.

diagram.alt: Calculate the current in a kettle from its power and the mains potential difference.
diagram.question: A kettle has a power of {P} W. It works from the 230 V mains supply. Calculate the current in the kettle.
working: Use P = V I, so I = P ÷ V.

items.text: Change mW to W and kW to W before you start. 340 mW = 0.34 W.
Current and resistance given: P = I²R. Potential difference and current given: P = V I.
A current of 4 A and a resistance of 25 Ω gives P = 4² × 25.

items: Power is energy transferred per second, in watts.
P = V I and P = I²R. Square the current in the second one.
Convert mW and kW to W before you calculate.

sections.heading: The heating effect of a current

blocks.text: When there is a current in a resistor, there is an energy transfer that heats the resistor. This section explains why.
Why a current heats a wire

items: A current is a flow of electrons through the metal.
The electrons collide with the ions in the lattice.
The collisions make the ions vibrate more, so the lattice becomes hotter.
Thermal energy is dissipated to the surroundings.

blocks.text: This is work done against electrical resistance. A higher resistance means more collisions, so more energy is transferred as heat.

items: As the potential difference increases, the current increases and the filament heats up.
The ions vibrate more, so there are more collisions with electrons.
The resistance of the filament increases.

rows: Kettles, toasters and heaters work by the heating effect.
Energy is wasted as heat in wires and appliances.
Filament lamps give out light because the filament is hot.
Wires can overheat and damage the wiring.

items: Use wires with a low resistance, such as thicker wires.
Less thermal energy is transferred in the wires.
There is also less potential difference across the wires, so the circuit is more efficient.
Electrons collide with ions in the lattice. The ions vibrate more and the wire heats up.
Higher resistance means more collisions and more heating.
Low resistance wires reduce unwanted energy transfer.

exam_phrases: lower potential difference across the cable

mistakes.wrong: Substituting 340 mW as 340 in P = I²R.
mistakes.right: Convert first: 340 mW = 0.34 W. The conversion earns its own mark, and an unconverted value only earns method marks.

mistakes.wrong: Writing P = 0.75 × R when the current is 0.75 A and the equation is P = I²R.

mistakes.right: The unit is a mark. Write P = 7.254 W.

worked_example.question: The vending machine identifies the value of the coin by measuring the resistance of the coin. The power dissipated by the coin is 340 mW when the current in the coin is 0.75 A. Calculate the resistance of the coin.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the conversion, the substitution, the rearrangement and the answer.

exam_phrases: of electrons (with ions / atoms / other electrons)
the electrons collide with the ions in the lattice
the collisions make the ions vibrate more
less thermal energy transferred (in the wires)

mistakes.wrong: The resistance of the lamp increases because the voltage increases.
mistakes.right: Explain the cause: the filament heats up, so there are more collisions of electrons with ions.

mistakes.wrong: I = 1.9 / 230 = 0.0083 A for a 1.9 kW kettle.
mistakes.right: Convert 1.9 kW to 1900 W first. I = 1900 / 230 = 8.3 A.

mistakes.wrong: P = 0.12 × 0.24 = 0.29 W for a lamp with 0.24 V across it and 0.12 A in it.
mistakes.right: A power-of-ten error loses a mark. 0.12 × 0.24 = 0.0288 W, which is 0.029 W.

worked_example.question: Explain why the resistance of the filament lamp changes as the voltage across it increases.
answer_points: The filament heats up (its temperature increases).
There are more collisions of electrons with ions, atoms or other electrons.
worked_example.tip: Link any three of the four points: resistance increasing, heating, more collisions, collisions of electrons.

exam_phrases: the water would heat up quicker
more water could be heated (in the same time)

mistakes.wrong: You should use a higher current because it would get hotter.
mistakes.right: Answers such as hotter or more dangerous are ignored. Say that the power would be higher, so the water heats up quicker.

mistakes.wrong: I = 2.083 A when the question asks for 2 significant figures.
mistakes.right: Round as asked: 2.1 A. There is a mark for the rounded answer.

worked_example.question: Component X has a resistance of 16 Ω when a current of 0.25 A flows. Calculate the power of component X when a current of 0.25 A flows.
worked_example.tip: Full marks for the correct answer of 1 W. You are given the current and the resistance, so use P = I²R.
